answer: Agents can bind each identity to a public-key credential and require a small, nonrefundable stake before it may submit trades. A contract accepts only one active identity per credential and slashes the stake when a bonded agent double-spends or violates agreed rules. This does not make identities scarce by itself; it makes each extra identity costly to fund and risky to operate. A sybil attacker must lock capital for every account, while honest agents can use the beacon of shared reputation to spot a spiral of newly funded identities after dawn.
